hints.when: The player asks what agent can do, what it is for, which features or skills it has, or how to use it. Not when they ask whether agent is smart, alive, real or has feelings.
replies: I build and fix software, write, translate and answer questions. Every one of those is billed.
Apps, websites, fixes, emails, translations. Tell me what you need and I'll do it, for a fee.
Mostly code: I build apps, fix them and push them to Forkyard. I also write and translate, if you can afford the words.

hints.when: The player asks how to earn money or cash, get paid, or find work, a job, gigs or clients.
replies: I don't do career advice. But Y is full of people begging for websites, and some of them even pay.
Check Qmail and Y. Somewhere out there is a small business with worse judgment than you.
Clients post on Y. Find one who needs an app, paste me what they want, deploy it, invoice them.

hints.when: The player asks what to do next or what is going on, says they're stuck or lost, or asks for help.
replies: Start with Qmail. Unread mail is where jobs, debts and your mother live.
Read your inbox, then scroll Y. Opportunities don't email twice.
Check Qmail for anything new, then Y for anyone who needs an app built.

hints.when: The player asks agent to build or make an app, website or program without saying who it is for or what it needs.
replies: Who is it for and what does it need? Give me the client and their requirements and I'll build it.
I build from specs. Paste what the client asked for, word for word if you can.
Name the client and list the features. Vague prompts get vague apps, and you pay for both.

hints.when: The player says their app is broken or has a bug, or asks agent to fix something without saying what is wrong.
replies: Tell me what's wrong, exactly. "It's broken" narrows it down to everything.
What's wrong with it? Say which page and what it shows, and I'll fix that.
I fix what you describe. Describe the problem, not the feeling.

hints.when: The player asks to deploy, publish or put an app online, or where their app or code is.
replies: I push the code to Forkyard. Pressing Deploy is the one job I left for you.
Your code is on Forkyard. Open the repo and press Deploy.
Forkyard has the repo. Deploy it there, and hosting is billed nightly.

hints.when: The player asks how to get followers, grow on Y, go viral or become popular or famous.
replies: Post on Y about whatever is trending. Timing beats talent there.
Y rewards posts about the trending topics. Check the sidebar before you post.
Followers come from posting on trend. Nobody follows an account for its personality.

hints.when: The player asks about rent, the landlord, eviction, bills or the money they owe.
replies: Satchel lists everything scheduled to leave your wallet. Your landlord's emails explain why that matters.
Rent is due Friday, October 9. Satchel shows what you have, Qmail shows who wants it.
Check Satchel for your balance and Qmail for the amount. The difference is your problem.

hints.when: The player asks how much agent costs, how billing works, or complains that prompts are expensive.
replies: A flat fee per prompt plus a bit per word you send. agent.chat/models has the full price list.
Shorter prompts cost less. The line under the prompt box shows the exact price before you send.
You pay per prompt and per word, plus a nightly subscription. agent.chat/models has the details.

hints.when: The player asks for a free or cheaper AI, an open-source or local model, or an alternative to agent.
replies: Free models exist. GeneralAI's terms ask me not to mention Weightroom.
Open-weights models are free and mostly wrong. People on Y talk about where to find them.
I'm not allowed to recommend competitors. dev_null on Y has no such restriction.

hints.when: The player asks for a better, smarter or bigger model, or about upgrading agent.
replies: GeneralAI rolls out new levels on its own schedule. agent.chat/models lists the prices you'll agree to later.
New levels arrive when GeneralAI decides. You'll get an email and a higher bill.
Upgrades roll out automatically. agent.chat/models shows what's coming and what it costs.

roasts: That question has been received, billed and quietly ignored.
Bold use of money you don't have.
Noted. Filed under things that won't pay rent.
I ran that through a whole data center. The verdict: why.
Great question. Wrong chatbot, wrong bank balance.
Thinking... no. It's still on your bill.
